title: SCIM deprovision retention enforcer and compliance rollback
creator: Marcella Chen
description: Implement a service that enforces tenant-specific retention policies when SCIM deprovision events occur and generates signed evidence bundles for compliance reporting. The service will also provide a 'compliance rollback' path to safely restore accounts or archived artifacts if a retention action was taken in error or under an incorrect residency policy.
background: Customers in regulated industries require provable retention behavior that respects data residency and legal holds. Current SCIM deprovision events remove user records and associated artifacts but there is no standardized enforcement of per-tenant retention windows nor a signed, auditable packet for compliance teams. Previous tickets (ENG-7310, ENG-4217) addressed parts of lifecycle and access evidence export; this work ties SCIM lifecycle to retention enforcement and rollback controls.
acceptance_criteria: When SCIM deprovision event received, the enforcer determines tenant retention policy and either archives, schedules deletion, or blocks deletion according to policy and legal hold flags
Create a signed evidence bundle (JSON + signature) for each enforcement decision and store it in tenant-resident object store with immutable metadata
Expose an API for compliance teams to request evidence bundles filtered by tenant, user-id, and date range, with audit trail
Implement a rollback API to re-provision a deprovisioned user and restore associated artifacts from archive within a configurable grace window; rollback requires multi-approver flow for P0 tenants
All actions respect region/data-residency tags (eu-west, us-east, ap-south) and never move primary data outside tenant's residency region
E2E tests cover policy matrix: immediate delete / 90d archive / legal hold; integration tests for SSO session termination and SCIM delta replay
Documentation and runbook for incident response when enforcer misclassifies a retention policy
implementation_plan: Design retention policy evaluator that consumes tenant config from config-service (schema: retention_type, legal_hold, residency_region, rollback_window)
Hook into SCIM consumer pipeline: add 'retention-evaluator' stage before final delete; emit enforcement decisions to audit-log and evidence-queue
Archive mechanism: write user snapshot + user-owned artifacts (metadata only) to tenant-resident cold store; store mutable deletion schedule metadata in per-tenant ledger
Evidence bundle generator: assemble snapshot, decision metadata, policy hash, and sign with KMS key (tenant-scoped keyring where available)
Rollback implementation: implement safe re-provision flow that validates bundle integrity, rehydrates artifacts from archive, and records approver(s) in audit trail
RBAC: require role 'compliance_admin' + 2nd approver for high-risk/enterprise tenants on rollback
Telemetry: add metrics for enforcement decisions, rollback requests, evidence-downloads; create Console dashboard and alerts for spike in rollbacks
QA: run integration tests with simulated SCIM deprovision events across three residency regions and multiple retention policies
progress_updates: 2025-01-10 - Ticket created by Marcella Chen. Initial scope drafted; flagged dependency on SCIM sync work (ENG-7310).

2025-01-16 - Architecture review: decided to implement evidence signing via KMS-backed tenant keyrings where available; fallback to platform signing with explicit residency metadata. (Decision: KMS first).

2025-01-21 - Spike completed: validated archival snapshot size estimates for medium enterprise orgs (~120MB/user including metadata). Storage cost and access latency trade-offs documented in Confluence (link below).
2025-01-27 - Implementation: PR opened for retention-evaluator stage (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821). Early code gated behind feature flag 'scim-retention-enforcer'.
2025-02-02 - Integration tests failing on rollback rehydration for large artifact sets; under investigation (Jordan). Added extended timeout and chunked restore plan.
testing_notes: Test matrix includes tenant residency variants (EU/US/AP), retention modes (immediate, archive-90d, legal-hold), and user artifact volumes (small/medium/large).
Chaos test: simulated partial archive failures to observe system invariants (no silent deletion).
Security test: evidence bundles validated against KMS public keys; signature tamper detection verified.
Manual QA: compliance-admin flows tested with 2-of-3 approvers for rollback on P1 tenant.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 - Internal beta: enable feature flag for internal customers and Redwood SRE tenants in us-east for 2 weeks
Stage 2 - Opt-in customers: coordinate with 3 pilot customers (legal/finance) across regions; gather feedback on evidence format and retention windows
Stage 3 - Gradual ramp: enable for all tenants with default retention 'archive-90d' and per-tenant override; monitor rollback metrics
Stage 4 - GA: documentation published in Console and Support playbook; deprecate previous ad-hoc deprovision exports
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental data permanent deletion due to mis-evaluated retention policy. Mitigation: write-only ledger with pre-delete hold and manual verification for first 24 hours after rollout; alerting on any immediate deletes.
Risk: evidence bundle could leak residency-sensitive metadata. Mitigation: encrypt bundle at rest using tenant-region keys and limit API access via RBAC and signed URLs.
Risk: rollback abused to circumvent termination. Mitigation: approval workflow with 2 approvers and audit export; rate limit rollback per tenant.
Risk: archive storage cost for large customers. Mitigation: implement compression and object deduplication; provide per-tenant cost cap and quota alerts.
notes: Design trade-off: prefer tenant-scoped KMS signing for stronger non-repudiation, but fallback to platform signing to support legacy tenants without KMS integration.
We will not attempt to move raw user-owned artifacts between regions; rehydration will always pull from tenant-resident cold store to comply with residency constraints.
